 Lansing sees surge in early voting ahead of Election Day as clerk details ballot security 
 City Clerk Chris Swope says early turnout has surpassed 4,000 voters, while 24-hour surveillance and police coordination protect ballot boxes across the capital city 
 By Danny Valle Published : Oct. 31, 2026 at 3:06 PM EDT | Updated : 2 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google LANSING, Mich. (News 10) - Early in-person voting is seeing a massive surge across the capital city heading into the final weekend before Election Day, with local election officials assuring residents that comprehensive safeguards are in place to keep every ballot secure.
 Lansing City Clerk Chris Swope reported that more than 4,000 residents have already cast their ballots early in person. Swope noted that turnout has surpassed every previous election cycle in Lansing’s history by a wide margin, trailing only the November 2024 presidential election.
 “I think there’s a lot of interest in this election, so I think people are wanting to turn out and vote,” Swope said.
 Alongside the high voter volume, city election staff and the Lansing Police Department have implemented layered security measures to safeguard ballots, drop boxes, and counting machinery. Every ballot bag and tabulator in the city is secured with serial numbers and tamper-evident seals to preserve a strict chain of custody.
 Swope emphasized that ballot drop boxes stationed throughout Lansing remain under constant watch, with law enforcement actively monitoring feeds.
 “There are cameras pointed at each one,” Swope said. “They are under 24-hour surveillance... and the police have access to those video cameras as well.”
 While election workers routinely take roughly two hours to collect ballots along city routes, Swope said a worker will be stationed at every single drop box across Lansing at 8 p.m. sharp on Election Night to collect the final ballots, lock the boxes, and attach closing notices.
 Addressing concerns over potential vandalism or tampering, Swope noted that Lansing has not experienced such incidents and warned that tampering with election infrastructure constitutes multiple felonies.
 Lansing voters have an additional day of early voting compared to most communities across Michigan.
 Under the state constitutional amendment allowing clerks discretion over voting schedules, Lansing residents can cast early ballots through Monday at 4 p.m. at two city locations, including 701 W. Jolly Road.
 Swope also issued a key reminder for absentee voters using drop boxes: ballots must be submitted into an official drop box designated for your specific city or township, otherwise they must be mailed to count.
